review_scope: All 76 hybrid baseline mismatches, independently reviewed against immutable texts, existing annotation policy and hackathon assignment; detector implementation was not inspected.
review_limitations: This is an independent AI review, not human adjudication or official organizer ground truth.
Classifications are recommendations; golden v1 and its uncertainty flags were not changed.
Case summaries deliberately distinguish label mismatch from objectively demonstrated privacy failure.
No held-out data was created; improvements informed by this audit remain in-sample.

external_primary_reference.scope: FTS describes 12 digits for individual INN and 10 digits for organizational INN. No personal-number lookup was performed.

policy_inconsistencies_or_underdetermina.finding: Same bare passport-like format, but org_0160 is negative solely because personal meaning is unconfirmed; positive cases also lack personal context. A trailing 00 is not enough to prove non-personal meaning.

Valid individual INN is negative without a label and positive with a label, whereas less-specific passport-shaped digits are often positive without labels. This is a policy asymmetry, not proof that the detector should expose an unlabeled INN.
Decimal suffix .0 is accepted as serialization for phone numbers but makes valid 12-digit INN examples negative under the current labels. A uniform suffix heuristic cannot satisfy both intents.
Unlabeled 16-digit number with Luhn sum 69 is assumed to be a card. The label does not demonstrate that arbitrary invalid card-shaped numbers should be detected.
Bare writer-name matches are public-person negatives; the same surname is personal in an heir context. Global name allowlists would be unsafe.
